title: Romans 1: Gentile wise men charged with exchanging God’s glory for corruptible image-likenesses
source_text: XVIII. Nec in veteri solum, sed in Novo quoque Testamento, crimini gentibus vertitur, quod Deum in imaginibus depingere ausi sint, & sub hominum forma, & diversorum animalium figuris repraesentare. Nam Paulus in epistola ad Romanos capite primo, gentium sapientes stultitiae in eo arguit, quod Mutaverunt gloriam incorruptibilis Dei, in similitudinem imaginis corruptibilis hominis, & volucrium, & quadrupedum, & serpentum.
pass_a_gloss: Nor in the Old only, but in the New Testament also, it is turned to the crime of the Gentiles that they dared to depict God in images, and to represent him under the form of men, and under the figures of diverse animals. For Paul in the epistle to the Romans chapter one argues the wise of the Gentiles of folly in this, that They exchanged the glory of the incorruptible God into the likeness of an image of corruptible man, and of birds, and of four-footed beasts, and of serpents.
pass_b_english: Romans 1 puts Gentile image-making under NT indictment, not OT ceremonial only.
Paul’s charge: swapping incorruptible God’s glory for likenesses of man, birds, beasts, and serpents.
